[MUQATIL:83:1-5/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | He warns that those who cheat in measure should consider whether they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p298/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The great day is the Resurrection; if the defrauders believed they would be resurrected, they would not cheat in measure or weight.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r15] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The إن clause and what it governs occupy the two object positions of يظن.
[SULAMI:v2p380#2/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · author | holds | Those addressed must face reckoning and return to God with their deeds.
[SULAMI:v2p380#2/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو حفص | reports | Someone who knows he will be raised and judged yet persists in sins acts as though he does not believe in resurrection and reckoning.
[THALABI:v10p151/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The question means that cheaters should know with certainty they will be raised for a tremendous day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds.
[THALABI:v10p151/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عمر | reports | A listener reports Ibn Umar weeping and falling when he recited the Day people stand before God, unable to continue.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Ala yaẓunnu means do they not know with certainty that the fraudulent will be resurrected for the great Day, the Resurrection.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r13] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · قيل | reports | Another view takes yadhunnu to mean certainty; al-Zamakhshari prefers the interpretation he gave earlier.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The passage turns to resurrection as a rebuke; this supports a Medinan setting involving believers while applying to the rest of the community too.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Here يظن means to know and be certain.
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | “The day people stand” is accusative, governed by “raised,” meaning the day they are resurrected.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p53/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj reasons that if the defrauders believed they would be resurrected, they would not reduce measures and weights.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One reading takes ẓann as knowledge; the addressees may be believing Aws and Khazraj, whom the Prophet reminded of their already-held belief in resurrection.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | On the same reading, even people who deny resurrection can be urged to infer it rationally from the need, or at least possibility, of recompense for good and evil.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Inferential knowledge can be called “supposition” because it rests on what is most probable, unlike doubt where both alternatives are equal.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A second reading takes ẓann literally: even without certainty, people should at least suspect a resurrection, since God's wisdom and mercy would not neglect them after death; that suspicion should suffice to make them fear.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | The soundest meaning of people standing for their Lord is standing for judgment, where trivial fraud is shown to have accumulated into a great wrong. | mentions 55:46
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Though the fraud is tiny, universal judgment displays God's wisdom: vindicating the wronged over even a small amount shows the precision of divine knowledge and justice.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another explanation is that God restores souls to bodies, and those bodies rise from their graves.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أبو مسلم | reports | Abū Muslim understands the standing as people standing in worship and obedience solely for God, like “stand for God devoutly.” | mentions 2:238, 82:19
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · النبي | reports | A report from Ibn ʿUmar quoting the Prophet says each person stands submerged in sweat up to half his ears.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عمر | reports | Ibn ʿUmar wept so intensely while reciting this verse that he could not continue.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · النبي | reports | A Prophetic report says the people stand for three hundred worldly years without being given any order.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd says they remain for forty years and are then addressed.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the standing lasts for believers only about as long as it takes them to finish a prayer.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The question rebukes traders for acting as if resurrection and accountability never occur; here zann means certainty.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | If they truly knew they would be resurrected, they would not reduce measure and weight.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Alternatively, if they doubt resurrection, they should at least consider it and investigate cautiously.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | An Arab rebuked ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan for taking Muslim property without measure, applying the threat to rulers too.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The rebuke, word “think,” great-day description, and people's submission show the gravity of fraud and injustice in all dealings and acts.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Anyone who believed in resurrection would not dare such offenses; the verse rebukes their behavior, even more so if they were certain.
[QASHANI:83:1-5/r4] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | They do not expect resurrection and judgment, when inner virtues and vices become visible and cannot be feigned or hidden, bringing shame and consequence.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The question admonishes them to recognize resurrection; it can mean being raised on a great day or being raised for that day's reckoning.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الفراء | reports | He takes يوم as a substitute for يوم عظيم; one transmitted reading puts it in genitive after ليوم, while Zayd ibn Ali reads it nominative, ‘that is a day.’
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | يظن can mean to know with certainty, or retain its ordinary sense of weighing or expecting.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The rebuke, the day's greatness, people's humbled standing before the Lord of all worlds, and the wording about His lordship all show the enormity of cheating.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | كلا rebukes the cheats for their conduct.
[SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The apparent reading is ألا as an exhortative particle urging them to consider, with ظن meaning certainty.
[SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | An alternative parses ألا as a negation particle preceded by the interrogative hamza.
[BURHAN:v3p344/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · أبو الفتح | reports | Abu al-Fath allows ظن to mean either certainty or its usual sense here; the latter is stronger, since even imagining the great resurrection should deter sin, all the more so certainty.
[BURHAN:v3p344/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | prefers | The author prefers the ordinary sense of ظن: mere awareness of the resurrection's enormity should restrain wrongdoing, so certain knowledge would do so more powerfully.
[BURHAN:v4p155/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · ابن مالك | reports | Ibn Malik says ظن is restricted to certainty.
[BURHAN:v4p155/r10] BURHAN, d. 794 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib defines ظن as a broad term spanning doubt and certainty: it is based on an indicator, reaching knowledge when strong and mere supposition when very weak.
[BURHAN:v4p155/r11] BURHAN, d. 794 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib says stronger ظن takes emphatic or light أن, whereas weak ظن takes إن with an imperfect; the first sense is praiseworthy and the second blameworthy.
[BURHAN:v4p155/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · غيره | reports | Other scholars say ظن can also mean doubt, citing the command to accept the women as believers if they are known to be so. | mentions 60:10
[BURHAN:v4p155/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Zarkashi's proposed reply is that علم retains its literal sense here and ايمان means verbal affirmation, so the cited verse need not show that ظن means doubt. | mentions 60:10
[BURHAN:v4p155/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | ظن can mean certainty because it contains an element of certainty; without that element it would be ignorance. Zarkashi cites several Qur'anic examples, including this verse. | mentions 2:46, 69:20, 75:28
[BURHAN:v4p155/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Zarkashi gives a contextual test: praiseworthy, rewarded ظن means certainty; blameworthy, threatened ظن means doubt.
[BURHAN:v4p155/r6] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | A ظن followed by light إن indicates doubt; examples include a couple's fear of failing to keep God's limits and the assumption that the Messenger would not return. | mentions 2:230, 48:12
[BURHAN:v4p155/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | A ظن followed by emphatic إن indicates certainty; Zarkashi cites the present verse and two other passages. | mentions 69:20, 84:3
[BURHAN:v4p155/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The emphatic إن marks certainty, while the light form signals its opposite; examples contrast علم أن with حسبوا ألا, where حسبان means doubt. | mentions 8:66, 47:19, 5:71
[BURHAN:v4p155/r9] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Zarkashi addresses ظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه as an apparent counterexample, explaining that إن is attached to

 the verb. | mentions 9:118
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو جعفر بن الزبير | reports | Ibn al-Zubayr links the warning to the record of every deed in 82:10 and the exact weighing of deeds in 21:47; fraud may seem small but is a major crime and merits a great warning. | mentions 82:10, 21:47
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their habitual vice follows from feeling safe from punishment and denying the final accounting; the rhetorical question suggests even a mere suspicion of resurrection should restrain them, since decisive proofs have been given.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Resurrection is a compelled awakening like rising from sleep, for the great day of gathering and accounting, when reward and punishment follow deeds; only God knows its full reality.
[BURSEVI:v10p283/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Inwardly, the limited self shortchanges the spirit in true, essential monotheism because it lacks capacity; that tawhid has no counterpart and should not be weighed, while formal monotheism is the self’s due from the spirit.
[BURSEVI:v10p283/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | ‘Do they not think?’ is an interrogative hamza with negation, not an alerting particle, since removing the latter would leave the meaning intact; it may also urge them to think.
[BURSEVI:v10p283/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The Day is immense and people will be reckoned for even a speck or mustard seed; mention of mere supposition intensifies the warning, since even weak belief would deter cheating, while believers need certainty.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The renewed question magnifies the enormity of their fraud: the initial hamza conveys denial and astonishment, joined to a negative la, rather than an introductory or attention-getting particle; “belief” retains its ordinary sense.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | “Those” points to the defrauders, highlighting their defining vice and setting them apart; its distance suggests how far they are from goodness and corruption, so the question denies they believe in resurrection.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The astonished question about resurrection supports taking the initial warning to address Muslims; sincere Muslims stopped cheating, whereas hypocrites did not. | mentions 83:1
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Ẓann means its usual sense: a preponderant belief that the event will occur, as in 45:32. | mentions 45:32
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The demonstrative “those” singles the cheaters out for public blame and makes their described trait a reason for the rebuke.
[TABATABAI:83:1-5/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The question rebukes and expresses astonishment; the far demonstrative distances the cheaters from God's mercy, and the Great Day is the Resurrection when they are repaid.
[ASAD-NOTES:83:4/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · Asad | holds | The wrongdoers are to be raised and called to account on the awesome Day when everyone stands before the Sustainer of all worlds.
[ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · Asad | reports | Authentic traditions cited by Tabari, Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir place at least the first four verses shortly after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r1] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · بعضهم | rejects | Some interpret lā in lā uqsim as negating the oath itself; the author rejects this in favor of denying the need to swear.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r2] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | holds | The Quranic formula denies God's need to swear, making the context itself attest to certainty and thereby affirming and establishing the message.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r3] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | holds | Ordinary Arabic similarly confirms trust by saying 'do not swear' or 'I need no oath,' just as 'I need not urge you' strengthens an instruction.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r4] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | holds | She says this study does not deny the early generations' service; their generous contribution has remained a store and support for later generations.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Sūrah al-Muṭaffifīn supplements al-Infiṭār, sharing its theme and elaborating the division of righteous and defiant people at its end.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Al-Infiṭār reasons from God’s attributes displayed in the human body, while this sūrah reasons from the moral nature God gave people.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Since God is just and created people with a love of justice, He must establish a day to reward those who honor that nature and punish those who disregard it.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Qur’an repeatedly uses this reasoning for the Day of Judgement; the author points to his discussion of 75:14–15. | mentions 75:14, 75:15
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Verses 1–6 censure people who demand fair treatment while cheating others; their conduct shows they do not expect to be raised before their Lord for judgement.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | This nature shows that people distinguish good from evil and expect different treatment; God must therefore judge righteous and wrongdoers, and the deniers resist because they wish to evade that outcome.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The question expresses wonder at disbelievers’ attitude: everyone should fear the great day attested by human nature, when people rise before the Creator and are judged and recompensed.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The phrase Lord of the worlds carries arguments for the majesty and necessity of the Day and its judgements, which the author has explained elsewhere.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r11] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Cheaters would not dare such fraud if they firmly believed, or even considered it possible, that they would be resurrected.
[STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The sūrah may be late Makkan, early Madinan, or a combination of both.
[STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2] STUDYQURAN · Bg, IK, Ṭ | reports | One account places the first four verses just after the Prophet arrived in Madinah, verses 5–28 in Madinah, and the final eight among the last verses revealed in Makkah.
